title: Mental Health in University/Work: A Self-Safety Net
summary: Transitioning to university/work brings new pressures: estrangement, performance, relationships, financial decisions. Your tools: (1) A consistent routine (sleep, movement, nutrition) — the chemical foundation for your brain. (2) A support network: a trusted friend, an academic mentor, a university counselor, a hotline (937). (3) Personal warning signs: write them down and monitor them weekly. (4) An emergency plan: 937/112, an emergency contact, a known psychiatrist. Independence means taking responsibility for your mental health.
try_this: This week: Write a personal "safety card" — 3 warning signs, 3 calming strategies, 3 people you trust + 937. Keep it in your wallet/phone.
reflection_prompts: What are the three warning signs you identified?
Who are the three people in your safety net?

review_defects.why: Arabic specifies a friend for emergencies, English generalizes to any contact.
